title: render badge
statement:
Python Engineer · Jinja2: templating done properly

Build render_badge

Import the badge macro from "macros.html" and render it. Output is escaped HTML.

Work through this step

  1. Read the contract and identify its boundary cases.
  2. Run the demonstration to explore the concept.
  3. Edit the module file; focus on this step’s function or class.
  4. Run required checks, then explain one design decision in Notes.
Hint

Start with the smallest example in the contract. Read the named failing test; separate the normal behavior from validation and edge cases. Related helpers share this module workspace.

Module concepts & examples

16 — Jinja2: templating done properly

Jinja2 renders HTML, emails, config files, SQL, YAML manifests, code generators — anywhere

you'd otherwise be gluing strings together. It's also the templating language behind

Flask, Ansible, dbt, Django-adjacent tooling and FastAPI's HTML responses.

In plain English

A template is a fill-in-the-blanks letter. You write the HTML once with gaps in it —

Hello {{ name }} — and hand it a name to fill in.

The thing worth genuinely caring about here is autoescaping, and it's a security idea,

not a formatting one.

Say a user sets their display name to <script>steal_cookies()</script>. If your template

drops that straight into the page, every visitor's browser will *run it*, because browsers

can't tell the difference between HTML you wrote and HTML a stranger typed into a form.

That's cross-site scripting, and it's been in the top 10 web vulnerabilities for two decades.

Autoescaping turns those dangerous characters into harmless ones automatically, so the name

displays as text instead of running as code. Jinja can do this for you on every single

variable — but only if you switch it on.

Watch out for: the |safe filter turns escaping *off* for one value. It exists for

markup you generated yourself. Using it on anything a user typed re-opens the exact hole

autoescaping just closed.

1. The three delimiters

{{ expression }}      {# printed  #}
{% statement %}       {# logic: if / for / set / block / macro / include #}
{# comment #}         {# never rendered #}

2. Environment and loaders — the part people skip

from jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader, select_autoescape

env = Environment(
    loader=FileSystemLoader("templates"),
    autoescape=select_autoescape(["html", "xml"]),   # SECURITY: see §5
    undefined=StrictUndefined,                       # fail loudly on typos
    trim_blocks=True,      # a block tag swallows the newline after it
    lstrip_blocks=True,    # ...and the leading whitespace before it
)
template = env.get_template("page.html")
html = template.render(user=user, items=items)

Loaders: FileSystemLoader, PackageLoader("mypkg", "templates") (works from a wheel),

DictLoader (tests), ChoiceLoader (overrides). Build one Environment per app and

reuse it — it compiles and caches templates.

Environment.from_string(...) is fine for one-offs and tests.

3. Control flow

{% for item in items %}
  {{ loop.index }}. {{ item.name }}{% if not loop.last %},{% endif %}
{% else %}
  Nothing here.        {# runs when `items` is empty — no equivalent in most languages #}
{% endfor %}

{% if user.is_admin %}...{% elif user.is_staff %}...{% else %}...{% endif %}
{% set total = items | sum(attribute="price") %}

loop gives you index (1-based), index0, first, last, length, revindex,

cycle("odd","even"), previtem/nextitem, and loop.depth for recursion.

4. Inheritance, includes, macros

{# base.html #}
<html><body>{% block content %}{% endblock %}</body></html>

{# page.html #}
{% extends "base.html" %}
{% block content %}
  {{ super() }}                  {# render the parent's version too #}
  <h1>{{ title }}</h1>
{% endblock %}
ToolUse
{% extends %} + {% block %}page layout (one parent per template)
{% include "part.html" %}drop in a fragment with the current context
{% macro %} / {% import %}reusable, parameterised components
{% call %}pass a body into a macro
{% macro field(name, value="", type="text") %}
  <input name="{{ name }}" value="{{ value }}" type="{{ type }}">
{% endmacro %}
{{ field("email", user.email) }}

Macros are the right answer to "I keep copying this markup". Includes are for whole

fragments, inheritance for page structure.

5. Autoescaping — the security section

Turn autoescaping on. With it off, {{ user_bio }} containing

<script>steal()</script> is an XSS hole.

Environment(autoescape=True)               # or select_autoescape([...])

- {{ value }} escapes < > & " ' when autoescape is on.

- {{ value | safe }} marks a value as already-safe HTML — only for content you

generated, never for user input.

- markupsafe.Markup("<b>ok</b>") is the programmatic equivalent.

- {% autoescape false %}...{% endautoescape %} scopes it off for e.g. plaintext email.

Never build HTML by concatenation and then pass it through |safe. That's the same hole

with more steps.

6. Filters and tests

{{ name | upper | truncate(20) }}
{{ price | round(2) }}
{{ items | selectattr("active") | map(attribute="name") | join(", ") }}
{{ description | default("none", boolean=true) }}
{{ raw_html | striptags }}
{% if value is defined and value is not none %}

Custom ones are just Python functions:

env.filters["currency"] = lambda v: f"${v:,.2f}"
env.tests["overdue"] = lambda task: task.due < today()
env.globals["now"] = datetime.now      # available in every template

That's the extension model in full: filters transform, tests answer yes/no, globals are

ambient values.

7. StrictUndefined

By default, {{ user.naem }} renders as an empty string — a typo becomes a silent blank

page. With undefined=StrictUndefined it raises UndefinedError. Use it everywhere

except templates that deliberately render optional data.

8. Async, streaming, sandboxing

- Environment(enable_async=True) → await template.render_async(...), needed under

FastAPI when a filter awaits.

- template.stream(...) / generate() yields chunks instead of one big string — for

large reports and CSV exports.

- SandboxedEnvironment when *users* supply templates. A normal Environment lets a

template reach __class__/__globals__ and escape to arbitrary code.

9. With FastAPI

from fastapi.templating import Jinja2Templates

templates = Jinja2Templates(directory="templates")

@app.get("/tasks", response_class=HTMLResponse)
async def page(request: Request):
    return templates.TemplateResponse(request, "tasks.html", {"tasks": tasks})

Keep logic in Python and presentation in the template. A template full of {% if %} is a

view model waiting to be extracted.

Exercises

exercises_16.py, then pytest 16_jinja2. You'll configure an environment properly,

write filters and macros, render an inheritance chain, and prove your autoescaping works.

Further reading

- Jinja2 template designer docs (optional reading: https://jinja.palletsprojects.com/en/stable/templates/)

- API docs (optional reading: https://jinja.palletsprojects.com/en/stable/api/)

Required check source
from dataclasses import dataclass

import pytest
from jinja2 import StrictUndefined, UndefinedError
from jinja2.exceptions import SecurityError

from courselib import impl

m = impl("16")


@dataclass
class Item:
    name: str


@dataclass
class Task:
    days_left: int


class TestEnvironment:
    @pytest.fixture
    def env(self):
        return m.build_environment({"greet.html": "hi {{ name }}"})

    def test_loader_is_wired(self, env):
        assert env.get_template("greet.html").render(name="ada") == "hi ada"

    def test_autoescape_on_for_html(self, env):
        assert env.get_template("greet.html").render(name="<b>") == "hi <b>"

    def test_strict_undefined(self, env):
        assert env.undefined is StrictUndefined
        with pytest.raises(UndefinedError):
            env.get_template("greet.html").render()

    def test_trim_and_lstrip(self, env):
        assert env.trim_blocks and env.lstrip_blocks

    def test_currency_filter(self, env):
        assert env.filters["currency"](1234.5) == "$1,234.50"
        assert env.filters["currency"](0) == "$0.00"

    def test_pluralise_filter(self, env):
        p = env.filters["pluralise"]
        assert p(1, "file") == "1 file"
        assert p(2, "file") == "2 files"
        assert p(0, "file") == "0 files"
        assert p(2, "box", "boxes") == "2 boxes"

    def test_overdue_test(self, env):
        assert env.tests["overdue"](Task(-1)) is True
        assert env.tests["overdue"](Task(3)) is False

    def test_site_name_global(self, env):
        assert env.globals["site_name"] == "Python Engineer"


class TestRenderString:
    def test_basic(self):
        assert m.render_string("{{ a }}+{{ b }}", a=1, b=2) == "1+2"

    def test_filters_available(self):
        assert m.render_string("{{ v | currency }}", v=5) == "$5.00"

    def test_globals_available(self):
        assert m.render_string("{{ site_name }}") == "Python Engineer"

    def test_strict(self):
        with pytest.raises(UndefinedError):
            m.render_string("{{ missing }}")

    def test_custom_test_available(self):
        out = m.render_string("{% if t is overdue %}late{% endif %}", t=Task(-2))
        assert out == "late"


class TestInvoice:
    @pytest.fixture
    def env(self):
        return m.build_environment({})

    def test_single_line(self, env):
        got = m.render_invoice(env, "ACME", [{"name": "Widget", "quantity": 2, "unit_price": 9.5}])
        assert got == (
            "INVOICE for ACME\n"
            "================\n"
            "Widget x2 @ $9.50 = $19.00\n"
            "----------------\n"
            "TOTAL: $19.00\n"
            "1 line"
        )

    def test_multiple_lines_and_total(self, env):
        lines = [
            {"name": "A", "quantity": 1, "unit_price": 10},
            {"name": "B", "quantity": 3, "unit_price": 2.5},
        ]
        got = m.render_invoice(env, "Co", lines)
        assert "A x1 @ $10.00 = $10.00" in got
        assert "B x3 @ $2.50 = $7.50" in got
        assert "TOTAL: $17.50" in got
        assert got.endswith("2 lines")

    def test_empty(self, env):
        got = m.render_invoice(env, "Nobody", [])
        assert "(no items)" in got
        assert "TOTAL: $0.00" in got
        assert got.endswith("0 lines")

    def test_no_trailing_newline(self, env):
        assert not m.render_invoice(env, "X", []).endswith("\n")

    def test_rule_widths(self, env):
        lines = m.render_invoice(env, "X", []).splitlines()
        assert lines[1] == "=" * 16
        assert "-" * 16 in lines

    def test_large_numbers_are_grouped(self, env):
        got = m.render_invoice(env, "X", [{"name": "N", "quantity": 1000, "unit_price": 12.5}])
        assert "TOTAL: $12,500.00" in got


class TestPage:
    def test_heading_in_h1(self):
        assert "<h1>Inventory</h1>" in m.render_page("Inventory", [])

    def test_items_rendered(self):
        html = m.render_page("Stock", [Item("keyboard"), Item("monitor")])
        assert "<li>keyboard</li>" in html
        assert "<li>monitor</li>" in html

    def test_empty_branch(self):
        assert "<li>empty</li>" in m.render_page("Stock", [])

    def test_title_uses_super_and_the_global(self):
        html = m.render_page("Stock", [])
        assert "<title>Stock · Python Engineer</title>" in html

    def test_inheritance_produced_a_full_document(self):
        html = m.render_page("Stock", [])
        assert html.strip().startswith("<html>")
        assert "</html>" in html

    def test_hostile_item_names_are_escaped(self):
        html = m.render_page("Stock", [Item("<script>steal()</script>")])
        assert "<script>steal()" not in html
        assert "<script>" in html

    def test_hostile_heading_is_escaped(self):
        assert "<img src=x" not in m.render_page("<img src=x onerror=1>", [])


class TestBadge:
    def test_default_kind(self):
        assert m.render_badge("new") == '<span class="badge badge-info">new</span>'

    def test_custom_kind(self):
        assert m.render_badge("late", "danger") == '<span class="badge badge-danger">late</span>'

    def test_escapes_text(self):
        assert "<b>" not in m.render_badge("<b>bold</b>")


class TestSandbox:
    def test_renders_normal_templates(self):
        assert m.render_untrusted("hello {{ name }}", name="ada") == "hello ada"

    def test_escapes_output(self):
        assert m.render_untrusted("{{ v }}", v="<b>") == "<b>"

    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        "attack",
        [
            "{{ ''.__class__ }}",
            "{{ ''.__class__.__mro__ }}",
            "{{ [].__class__.__base__.__subclasses__() }}",
            "{{ config.__class__.__init__.__globals__ }}",
        ],
    )
    def test_blocks_escapes(self, attack):
        with pytest.raises(SecurityError):
            m.render_untrusted(attack, config={})

    def test_a_normal_environment_would_have_leaked(self):
        # Contrast: proving the sandbox is doing something.
        leaked = m.render_string("{{ ''.__class__.__name__ }}")
        assert leaked == "str"

Review your understanding

What invariant does your implementation preserve? Which edge case would a simpler implementation miss?

Required checks assess your code. Benchmark timings and written reasoning are reported separately. Files are shared by this module’s steps; editing them makes those steps need verification again.
